explanation: Israel's patriarch, father of twelve sons who became the ancestors of Israel's twelve tribes.
A land in North Africa where Jacob's son Joseph was sold as a slave and later became a powerful ruler.
A shortage of food that led Jacob's family to travel to Egypt to buy grain.
The twelve sons of Jacob, including Joseph who was in Egypt.
Jacob's youngest son and Joseph's full brother; the brothers had to take him to Egypt to prove their honesty.
One of Jacob's sons who was held as a hostage in Egypt until the brothers returned with Benjamin.
The metal that the brothers found in their sacks after their first visit to Egypt, which created fear of accusations of theft.
A meal arranged by Joseph for his brothers, which surprised them since they expected punishment.
An object that Joseph placed in Benjamin's sack to test the brothers' loyalty and honesty.
